summary: Implementation Design froze the /argo-init validator bootstrap slice into stable contracts, a single read-only explicit entrypoint, and critical architecture guardrails. The explicit entrypoint now executes and fails for the intended missing package.json seeding behavior, which becomes the primary Coding/Repair target.

explicitEntrypoints.controlPoint: Run npm run test:explicit:argo-init-validator-bootstrap so the entry launches an extension host, invokes the exported /argo-init command handler, and drives bootstrap against a temporary workspace.
explicitEntrypoints.observationPoint: Observe the temporary workspace for copied validator assets, copied schema assets, package.json creation, and seeded validate:handoff scripts.
explicitEntrypoints.failureReason: The executable entry fails with AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected /argo-init to create package.json when it is absent.

criticalNonExplicitTests.name: commands-entry-boundary
criticalNonExplicitTests.controlPoint: Run npm run test:architecture:commands-entry-boundary to inspect src/commands and its contract fixture alignment.
criticalNonExplicitTests.observationPoint: Observe that every required command entry file exists, remains declared in src/commands/ARCHITECTURE.md, and avoids forbidden engine/model imports.

criticalNonExplicitTests.name: argo-init-explicit-entry-correctness
criticalNonExplicitTests.controlPoint: Run npm run test:architecture:argo-init-explicit-entry-correctness to inspect the explicit entry files and their contracts.
criticalNonExplicitTests.observationPoint: Observe that the explicit contract, command contract, entry file, and suite file all exist and remain linked to the ARGO-INIT-VALIDATOR-BOOTSTRAP-CONTRACT testcase.

criticalNonExplicitTests.name: validator-bootstrap-traceability
criticalNonExplicitTests.controlPoint: Run npm run test:architecture:validator-bootstrap-traceability to inspect the bundled validator assets, the repository shim, the npm manifest, and the related contracts.
criticalNonExplicitTests.observationPoint: Observe that the bundled validator script, shim, package.json scripts, and architecture contracts remain mutually traceable.

criticalNonExplicitTests.name: workspace-bootstrap-dependency-direction
criticalNonExplicitTests.controlPoint: Run npm run test:architecture:workspace-bootstrap-dependency-direction to inspect src/utils/workspaceBootstrap.ts imports and its local contract.
criticalNonExplicitTests.observationPoint: Observe that workspaceBootstrap.ts does not import commands, engine, or lm internals and that the utils contract keeps the package.json seeding gap explicit.

supportingNonExplicitTests.name: workspace-bootstrap-e2e
supportingNonExplicitTests.controlPoint: Run npm run test:e2e:workspace-bootstrap to launch the extension host on a temporary workspace and execute the manual bootstrap helper path.
supportingNonExplicitTests.observationPoint: Observe that activation does not auto-bootstrap and that the manual bootstrap path still copies the bundled validator and schema assets.

codingTargets.failureSignal: The explicit entry fails because /argo-init does not create package.json when the target workspace lacks one.
codingTargets.nextAction: Implement package.json seeding in workspaceBootstrap.ts so /argo-init creates a minimal manifest when absent and adds only the missing validate:handoff scripts without overwriting existing same-name scripts.

codingTargets.failureSignal: The explicit acceptance contract now expects /argo-init to surface the package.json bootstrap policy through the command path rather than through a hidden helper-only convention.
codingTargets.nextAction: Keep /argo-init as the stable orchestration entry while making any newly implemented package.json seeding behavior observable through this command path and its explicit test entry.

openGaps: The current bootstrap implementation still lacks package.json seeding and therefore leaves the explicit acceptance entry in an expected-failing state.
The current intent graph still does not embed formal explicit testcase objects, so the explicit entry is traced through the handoff artifact rather than a graph-local testcase object.
The selected Argo-managed path overwrite policy is frozen in contracts but still needs full code-level enforcement and future regression coverage when coding begins.
